items.date_basis: First repository addition; displayed calendar date America/New_York
items.title: ElMerFold accelerates protein-structure training-data generation on El Capitan
participants: LLNL (Brian Van Essen, Nikoli Dryden, Tal Ben-Nun)
items.what_changed: Reports more than 10,700 predicted protein structures per second on 45,200 MI300A APUs, 71.7-fold speedup over an extrapolated baseline, and estimated generation of approximately 41 million structures in 2.5 hours instead of eight days. Gordon Bell finalist; winner not yet announced.
items.significance: Accelerates synthetic training-data production for open biomolecular models and antibody-antigen prediction. Substantive performance update beyond earlier roughly 2,400 structures/second report.
items.affiliation_evidence: LLNL's new article and official ElMerFold project page describe OpenFold distillation and NNSA mission applications without project-specific Genesis attribution. Checked DOE RFA roster, repository project records, LLNL's ten-project Genesis announcement and targeted ElMerFold/OpenFold searches. LLNL's BIND metalloprotein project and common biology themes do not document affiliation for ElMerFold.
items.deduplication_note: Absent from archive and accessible review records; syndicated copies suppressed. Preserve timestamp from this review-repository addition if subsequently published.
items.summary: LLNL, AMD and Columbia report more than 10,700 protein-structure predictions per second on El Capitan, accelerating training-data generation for OpenFold3. The work could speed development of open biomolecular models. No project-specific Genesis Mission affiliation has been verified.
